topic.title: Food: A small bakery helps the neighborhood
topic.focus: A small bakery helps the neighborhood

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-5. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: An old building becomes a bakery
sections.text: In 2015, Maria buys an old building in her neighborhood. She is 30 years old. She loves to bake bread. The neighborhood is poor. There is no good bakery. Maria wants to change this.

sections.heading: Fresh bread every day
sections.text: Maria opens her bakery in 2016. She wakes up at 4 in the morning. She makes fresh bread. At 6, the bakery opens. People line up to buy warm bread. The bread is good and not expensive.

sections.heading: More than bread
sections.text: Maria teaches young people to bake. Three students learn from her every week. They learn to make bread, cakes, and pastries. It is good work. When they learn enough, they can work in a bakery and earn money.

sections.heading: The neighborhood changes
sections.text: Many people eat Maria's bread. Families feel proud. They have good food. The street looks nice now. More shops open nearby. People come to the bakery and shop in other stores. The neighborhood is alive again.

sections.heading: A dream comes true
sections.text: Now Maria has two bakeries. She employs 12 people. She gives jobs to poor young people. They have hope now. Maria says baking is not just about bread. It is about giving people work and dignity.

passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — An old building becomes a bakery
In 2015, Maria buys an old building in her neighborhood. She is 30 years old. She loves to bake bread. The neighborhood is poor. There is no good bakery. Maria wants to change this.

Paragraph 2 — Fresh bread every day
Maria opens her bakery in 2016. She wakes up at 4 in the morning. She makes fresh bread. At 6, the bakery opens. People line up to buy warm bread. The bread is good and not expensive.

Paragraph 3 — More than bread
Maria teaches young people to bake. Three students learn from her every week. They learn to make bread, cakes, and pastries. It is good work. When they learn enough, they can work in a bakery and earn money.

Paragraph 4 — The neighborhood changes
Many people eat Maria's bread. Families feel proud. They have good food. The street looks nice now. More shops open nearby. People come to the bakery and shop in other stores. The neighborhood is alive again.

Paragraph 5 — A dream comes true
Now Maria has two bakeries. She employs 12 people. She gives jobs to poor young people. They have hope now. Maria says baking is not just about bread. It is about giving people work and dignity.
